title: A hard time limit runs the failure path twice: the link_error errback runs twice and task_failure is sent twice; with task_acks_on_timeout off the task is failed (errback, FAILURE) and also requeued, and runs again
where: request.py:539-614 and 745-796 (celery 768e476, the same at 9c2f238): billiard calls the error callback (Request.on_failure with TimeLimitExceeded) and then the timeout callback (Request.on_timeout); each calls mark_as_failure (the errbacks) and sends task_failure; on_failure skips the store when it requeues, on_timeout does not. The second task_failure came with celery PR 10226 (closes celery issue 10194) in 5.7.0; the second errback call is older: on 5.4.0 and 5.5.3 a hard limit already calls the errback twice and sends task_failure once (the lead's rerun). tasks.rst:1140-1153 says on_failure, errbacks and task_failure are invoked as for a soft limit; configuration.rst:705-719 says a timed-out message is rejected and requeued when task_acks_on_timeout is off. No upstream thread found (searched time limit errback twice, TimeLimitExceeded link_error twice, task_failure signal twice, hard time limit task_failure, errback called twice, acks_on_timeout requeue; closest celery issue 4827, task_failure not sent on a time limit, and celery issue 10194); not in the tracker yet
thread: none yet (a new issue, or a comment on celery PR 10226; the lead decides)
observed: 9c2f238 with kombu 445027e, billiard 4.3.2, redis-py 8.1.0, Redis 7 broker and backend, one prefork worker -c 1, acks_late, a task with time_limit=1 and a link_error errback; nothing injected. hard (sleeps 5 s): 3 of 3 runs (and 1 of 1 in a first probe) the errback ran twice and task_failure was sent twice, Task.on_failure and after_return once, FAILURE stored, the message acked; the log has "Task handler raised error: TimeLimitExceeded(1)" and then "Hard time limit (1s) exceeded". noackto (task_acks_on_timeout = False; the first run sleeps 5 s, the second returns): 3 of 3 the errback, task_failure and on_failure ran once with FAILURE stored, then the requeued message ran again and the state became SUCCESS (after_return saw FAILURE, then SUCCESS). Control raise (a task that raises): 3 of 3 each hook once, FAILURE. Natural rate: every hard time limit, no timing involved. The lead reran it on 9c2f238 and it holds; on 5.4.0 and 5.5.3 the errback runs twice and task_failure is sent once.
